samf-senior-2005-r1-03.title: Angle chase
samf-senior-2005-r1-03.body:
$\angle AFE=180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ$. $AC$ is a diagonal of the square, so $\angle FAE=45^\circ$. In triangle $AEF$: $\angle AEF=180^\circ-60^\circ-45^\circ=75^\circ$.

**Answer: (D) $75^\circ$**

samf-senior-2005-r1-04.title: Half the rectangle minus the notch
samf-senior-2005-r1-04.body:
The shaded region is the part above the diagonal of a $10\times12$ rectangle, which is half of it, $60$, with a $4\times4$ square removed from the corner: $60-16=44$.

**Answer: (C) 44**

samf-senior-2005-r1-06.title: Negative product
samf-senior-2005-r1-06.body:
A negative product needs one negative and one positive number. The most negative is $-8\cdot4=-32$ (the choice $-40=-8\cdot-5$ would not be negative; it equals $+40$).

**Answer: (B) $-32$**

samf-senior-2005-r1-07.title: Circumference
samf-senior-2005-r1-07.body:
The circumference is $2\pi\cdot0.7=1.4\pi\approx1.4\cdot\frac{22}7=4.4$ m. The number of revolutions is $100\div4.4\approx22.7\approx23$.

**Answer: (E) 23**

samf-senior-2005-r1-09.title: Counterexample
samf-senior-2005-r1-09.body:
Take $x=0.1$, $y=0.9$: $(x-y)^2=0.64>x^2=0.01$, so (A) fails. The others always hold: $0<y-x<y$ gives (B); $x<y$ gives (C); $x^3-y^3<0<x^2$ gives (D); $y^3-x^3<y^3$ since $x^3>0$ gives (E).

**Answer: (A)**

samf-senior-2005-r1-10.title: Cut into triangles
samf-senior-2005-r1-10.body:
Cut the hexagon into six congruent equilateral triangles from its centre. The shaded region is one and a half of them, so the proportion is $\frac{1.5}{6}=\frac14$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac14$**

samf-senior-2005-r1-11.title: Pairs of numbers
samf-senior-2005-r1-11.body:
Each number $n$ in the top line sits above $n+1$ in the bottom line. For $n$ from $20$ to $29$ the units digits differ, and the tens digits agree for $n=20,\dots,28$ (nine of the ten; $29$ and $30$ differ). The same holds for each of the four groups of ten, so the total is $9\times4=36$.

**Answer: (B) 36**

samf-senior-2005-r1-12.title: Count ends
samf-senior-2005-r1-12.body:
There are $2n$ ends. Adam picks one; this leaves $2n-1$ ends for Brian, exactly one of which belongs to the same rope. The probability is $\frac1{2n-1}$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac1{2n-1}$**

samf-senior-2005-r1-14.title: Count
samf-senior-2005-r1-14.body:
The two non-zero digits, in order, form one of $6$ ordered pairs with sum $7$: $(1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1)$. The zeros can then be placed in $3$ ways, since the first digit must be non-zero: $ab00$, $a0b0$, $a00b$. Total $6\times3=18$.

**Answer: (E) 18**

samf-senior-2005-r1-16.title: Name the areas
samf-senior-2005-r1-16.body:
The six triangles are $APQ,APR,APS,AQR,AQS,ARS$. Let $[APQ]=x$ and $[ARS]=y$. $AQR$ is the smallest, area $1$, and $APS$ the largest, of area $4$: $x+1+y=4$, so $x+y=3$. The areas are $x,\ x+1,\ 4,\ 1,\ 1+y,\ y$, with sum $3(x+y)+4=13$. The average is $\frac{13}6$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac{13}6$**

samf-senior-2005-r1-17.title: Sums of rows
samf-senior-2005-r1-17.body:
The last numbers of the rows are $1,5,11,19,\dots$, which are $n^2+n-1$: indeed row $n$ ends at the $\frac{n(n+1)}2$-th odd number, $2\cdot\frac{n(n+1)}2-1=n^2+n-1$. For $n=80$: $6400+80-1=6479$.

**Answer: (A) 6479**

samf-senior-2005-r1-18.title: Equations
samf-senior-2005-r1-18.body:
Let the present ages be $A,B,C$: $A=3(C+1)$, $B+12=3A$, $B=8C$. Then $8C+12=9(C+1)$, so $C=3$, $A=12$, $B=24$.

**Answer: (C) 24**

samf-senior-2005-r1-19.title: 30-60-90 triangle
samf-senior-2005-r1-19.body:
The centres lie on the bisector of angle $R$. Take the right-angled triangle with a vertex at each centre and with sides parallel to $QR$ and $PQ$: it has an angle of $30^\circ$ at $R$. If the larger radius is $r$, the hypotenuse (joining the centres) is $r+1$ and the shortest side (parallel to $PQ$) is $r-1$. In a $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle the hypotenuse is twice the shortest side: $r+1=2(r-1)$, so $r=3$.

**Answer: (D) 3**

samf-senior-2005-r1-20.title: Count the smokers with cancer
samf-senior-2005-r1-20.body:
Let $\ell\%$ of the population have lung cancer. The smokers with lung cancer make up $10\%$ of the $20\%$ who smoke, i.e. $2\%$ of the population, and also $90\%$ of $\ell\%$. So $0.9\ell=2$ and $\ell=\frac{20}9$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac{20}9$**
